title: ～て / ～で — joining clauses with the te-form
summary: The te-form links clauses: actions in order (食べて、走った), a reason (風邪をひいて、休んだ), or listed features (安くて、おいしい). I-adjectives use ～くて; na-adjectives and nouns use ～で.

body.p: Sequence (食べて、走る), cause or reason (風邪をひいて、休んだ), and listing (安くて、おいしい). Context tells which is meant.
The tense is set by the final predicate. Do not put た on the earlier part (× 食べたて).

examples.ja: 風邪（かぜ）をひいて、学校（がっこう）を休（やす）みました。
examples.romaji: Kaze o hiite, gakkō o yasumimashita.
examples.tr: I caught a cold and was absent from school.

examples.ja: 朝（あさ）ご飯（はん）を食（た）べて、公園（こうえん）を走（はし）りました。
examples.romaji: Asa gohan o tabete, kōen o hashirimashita.
examples.tr: I ate breakfast and then ran in the park.

examples.ja: この店（みせ）は安（やす）くて、料理（りょうり）もおいしいです。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa yasukute, ryōri mo oishii desu.
examples.tr: This restaurant is cheap and the food is delicious too.

pitfalls: After a reason-て you cannot put a request, command or intention (× 忙しくて手伝ってください).
Keep the earlier clause tenseless; only the last predicate takes the past.
